title: Strong and trustworthy
hook: the best to hire is the strong and the trustworthy (28:26)
carry: the kind of job nobody will check

segments.voice: Yesterday: haya', modesty you can see in a walk. Your line was modesty is a walk.

Every hiring manager has a list: experience, references, a good interview. Musa has none of it. He's a fugitive with no money, no letters, no home, sitting in a stranger's house in Madyan. He has told the old man his whole story, and the old man has said, don't be afraid, you've escaped from the wrongdoing people. Then one of the daughters speaks up and gives him a reference. Two words, and she has seen him earn both.

Hire him, she tells her father. Pickthall: "the best (man) that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy." In Arabic, al-qawiyy al-amin. Qawiyy is strong, able to do the work. Amin is trustworthy, from the same root as amana, a trust, and iman, faith. She has seen both. Strength at the well, where he watered a whole flock that had been waiting behind the shepherds. Trustworthiness on the way home: commentators tell, from a report attributed to 'Umar, that Musa asked her to walk behind him and call out the way, so he wouldn't be looking at her as she walked. That detail is from commentary, not the verse. Either way, she'd watched him work, and watched him behave when no one else was looking. Both words matter. Strength without trust is a danger: a capable person you can't rely on. Trust without strength is a disappointment: a good person who can't do the job. The same pair turns up once more, in Surah An-Naml, from an unlikely mouth: a jinn offering to fetch the Queen of Sheba's throne says he is strong and trustworthy for the job. The old man takes his daughter's advice. He offers Musa marriage to one of his daughters, for eight years of work, or ten if he chooses. Musa answers: whichever term I complete, let there be no injustice to me. A contract between two people who each had reason to trust the other. A hadith in Bukhari warns that when trust is lost, the Hour is near.
screen: `AL-QAWIYY AL-AMIN.` · `STRENGTH SEEN AT THE WELL.` · `TRUST SEEN ON THE WALK HOME.` · `BOTH, OR NEITHER IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Think of the work in front of you today, paid or unpaid: a job, a class, a household, caring for someone. Ask honestly where you're strong but not quite trustworthy, a corner cut, a promise let slide, and where you're trustworthy but not yet strong. If you pray, you can ask for strength and trust together.
Al-amin. The daughter's word for Musa: trustworthy, safe to trust with the work. Today's word.
Your line: the kind of job nobody will check. Trust shows when no one is watching. See you tomorrow, then.

howItsDone: Muslims often cite 28:26 when speaking of hiring, leadership and work ethic, holding that a person given a role should be both capable and trustworthy.

original.note: Arabic: the strong, the trustworthy; the daughter's words for Musa in 28:26.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice compliment.
what it means: a two-part test for anyone given a job: able to do it, and safe to trust with it.
what a scholar hears: al-qawiyy al-amin, the same pair a jinn claims for himself in 27:39; amin from a-m-n, the root of amana and iman; and the hadith that lost trust signals the Hour (Bukhari 59).
recall: a sound heart, brought to God

chat.says: What did the daughter see in Musa that made her say hire him?
options: Strength at the well, and trustworthiness: both together, al-qawiyy al-amin.
Strength mostly; being trustworthy matters less if you can do the job.
Good references from Egypt, since he grew up in Pharaoh's household.
chat.meaning: 28:26: the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy. She had seen his strength at the well and his conduct on the way.

amana.meaning: a trust, something left in your care

notes: Pickthall 28:26 quoted from memory; confirm wording.
The 'walk behind me' detail is reported in tafsir (e.g. Ibn Kathir, via a report from 'Umar); labeled as commentary. Confirm.
The old man of Madyan is not named in the Qur'an; many identify him with Shu'ayb, others disagree. The script leaves him unnamed.

Audit: the teach claimed Surah Yusuf (12:55) pairs 'strong' and 'trustworthy', but Yusuf's words there are 'careful guardian, knowing'; replaced with 27:39, where qawiyy and amin actually recur, and updated the trapdoor and sources. Also cut the unsourced 'shortest job recommendation in scripture' line from the hook.
